page: Microsoft Azure D64ls_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the Dlsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by a 480 MB L3 cache. The system is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage is bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and instruction-level performance. The server achieved a top-tier PassMark CPU score of 87,182.31 and a strong multi-core stress-ng score of 68,669.54. Memory bandwidth is notable, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 5,133.04 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 128.5 GB/sec. The processor's support for advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions), is reflected in strong performance for extended instructions and cryptography. Additionally, the instance demonstrated strong prompt processing speeds for LLM inference across small, medium, and large models, though text generation speeds remained average.

The primary trade-off of the D64ls_v7 is its low memory density of 2.0 GB per vCPU and the complete absence of local storage. This hardware profile optimizes cost efficiency for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local disk space, avoiding the premium associated with high-memory configurations. It is highly suitable for multi-threaded computational tasks, static web serving, database operations, cryptography, and batch processing workloads like bzip3 decompression.
